findings.problem: The identity boundary permits exactly one named approver using a shared Basic credential and explicitly prohibits multi-user approval, but the required pilot gate has three managers use the queue and measures their actions and ratings. The document neither limits the additional managers to read-only observation nor introduces individual identity before that gate, so it cannot safely attribute three managers' review states, approvals, or usefulness ratings under the committed pilot architecture.
findings.remedy: Choose an executable sequence: either keep the success gate to the single authenticated manager, define the other two managers as supervised read-only evaluators whose feedback is captured outside product audit claims, or make individual authentication and per-manager audit attribution a dependency before the three-manager pilot begins. Align Constraints, Identity Boundary, Success Criteria, Dependencies, and the Assignment to that choice.

findings.problem: The exception lifecycle enumerates only open, acted_on, dismissed, corrected, and unclear, but later says resolved triggers close an exception. There is no closed or resolved state, no transition into it, and no rule for what happens to prior acted_on, corrected, or unclear review history when a source change removes and later recreates the trigger.
findings.remedy: Define the missing resolved or closed state and a complete transition table driven by review actions, source changes, dismissal expiry, and trigger recurrence. Specify whether a recurring trigger reopens the same exception or creates a new occurrence while preserving the prior review and Task linkage.

findings.problem: The uniqueness constraint on proposal ID plus version makes retries of one displayed proposal idempotent, but it does not prevent two regenerated proposal IDs for the same exception, normalized intent, owner, and due-date window from creating duplicate Tasks. The document says proposals are bound to those logical fields but never makes that binding an atomic uniqueness scope, and it still gives no retention or expiry rule for deduplication records.
findings.remedy: Define a canonical logical-operation key from the company deployment, exception occurrence, Task type, owner, normalized intent, and due-date bucket; enforce it atomically across proposal IDs where duplicates are forbidden. State when a distinct follow-up is allowed, how edits affect the key, and how long proposal outcomes and deduplication keys remain authoritative.

findings.problem: The first slice calls Task creation reversible and promises to show the exact mutation, but it never defines the allowed Task payload, server-owned versus model-drafted fields, content and length constraints, due-date calculation, or how an approved Task is reversed when deletion and other mutations are outside the pilot. Rejecting unknown fields does not define the safe values of known fields.
findings.remedy: Specify the first-slice Task schema and validation contract, including fixed activity type, owner rules, subject and description limits, permitted model-authored text, due-date boundaries, escaping and display behavior, and immutable source linkage. Either define an authorized cancel or archive path with audit behavior or stop describing Task creation as reversible.

findings.problem: The approval design says provider metadata has bounded retention but supplies no duration, deletion trigger, or relationship to the longer-lived approval and exception audit records. This leaves the prior audit-retention obligation unresolved and prevents the pilot company from approving a concrete data lifecycle.
findings.remedy: Define retention periods and deletion behavior separately for proposal payloads, provider metadata, approval attempts and outcomes, exception-review events, deduplication keys, and reconciliation records. State which records must outlive the pilot for financial or security audit purposes and which are purged on a schedule.

findings.problem: The quotation rule says an expired valid_until date is an actionable trigger while also listing expired quotations among excluded records. A reader can infer that one means a date condition and the other a status value, but the contract does not say so, making the same word both included and excluded in a supposedly deterministic financial rule.
findings.remedy: Distinguish field semantics explicitly: for example, include an allowed-status quotation whose valid_until date is before the local date, while excluding records whose normalized status equals Expired. Add an example covering that exact distinction and define precedence when status and date disagree.

prior.evidence: Pilot Identity and Authorization Boundary now limits the deployment to one company and one named manager, assigns the configured administrator as the audit actor, prohibits additional approvers, and states the authentication and tenancy work required before expansion.

AI Data and Prompt-Injection Boundary now supplies an analysis allowlist, excludes unrestricted free text and direct identifiers, requires provider-policy acceptance, delimits any future text, and rejects unknown references, owners, activities, fields, dates, actions, and records before display.

Ranking and Visibility Contract requires the full deterministic set and count to remain accessible, prohibits AI membership or severity changes, provides a deterministic-order switch, exposes rationale and provenance, and rejects count mismatches.

Exception Review Lifecycle adds review states, permissions, reasons, expiry, non-mutating correction, and audit fields, but it says resolved triggers close an exception without defining a closed state or complete recurrence transitions.

Success Criteria now defines discovery, two-week pilot, AI-added-value, iterate, and stop gates with thresholds for precision, comprehension, action, correction, duplicate or unsafe proposals, and measured time saving.

Recommended Approach, Success Criteria, Dependencies, and the Assignment consistently stage one-manager discovery before a three-manager two-week pilot; the separate inability to execute the later gate under the stated identity model is tracked as R2-1.

Current-State Inventory maps records, authoritative fields, links, current support, and first-slice disposition, while Target User and Recommended Approach restrict implementation to quotation follow-up and Tasks.

quotation-follow-up/v1 now defines timezone behavior, included and excluded states, trigger boundaries, owner and missing-data behavior, stable ordering, rule version, and examples; later families are explicitly blocked on equivalent approved contracts.

Proposal Idempotency and Approval State Machine defines immutable IDs, versions, stale edits, retry outcomes, and proposal binding, but uniqueness remains proposal-ID-plus-version and therefore does not deduplicate regenerated proposals for the same logical Task; retention is also unspecified.

The approval state machine now durably records receipt, atomically commits Task creation with success, records rejections, and reconciles crashes, but the promised bounded provider-metadata and audit retention policy still has no concrete lifecycle.

Target User and Narrowest Wedge reduces the first vertical slice to one quotation-follow-up rule, one named manager, and Task creation only; later rule families and activity types are gated on measured expansion thresholds.
